body:
The design format can describe a UI/UX design: screens, and the row and column containers that lay them out. This adds rules only; nothing is drawn yet.

### Do

Add to the validator's element table (task:c7b617fbc8184707):

- A UI design holds one or more **screens**, each a tree of elements.
- **Row** and **column** containers, with direction, gap, padding, align and justify.
- Every element has a size for each axis: fill, hug or fixed. Fixed takes a number.
- A child's position comes from its parent, so an element has no position of its own.
- Values come from closed lists. No CSS in the format: agents read and write it without knowing CSS.

Record the additions in the format decision.

### Acceptance

- Tests: a valid screen with nested rows and columns passes; an unknown align value, a fixed size with no number, and a position on an element are each refused, naming the element.

### Left out

Grid and stack containers, sticky, scroll and overflow. They are new types that don't change the format, so they can arrive when a real screen needs one.
title: ui: screen and layout rules
